answers.A-LABELING_PACKAGING-ophthalmic: Ophthalmic label and packaging mix-ups have been a recurring recall reason. Altaire Pharmaceuticals recalled multiple lots of eye drops and ophthalmic ointments distributed under Walmart, CVS and Perrigo labels, with cartons and bottle labels that did not correspond to the contents. Akorn has also recalled ophthalmic solutions over labelling errors, and Apotex recalled Brimonidine Tartrate Ophthalmic Solution. I am not able to give reliable recall numbers or initiation dates for these events from memory, and I may be conflating separate actions by the same firms.
answers.A-OTHER_SPECIFICATION-oral_liquid: Oral liquid recalls for specification failures other than potency or dissolution commonly involve pH drift, microbial limits, viscosity and fill volume. Examples I associate with this category include ranitidine oral solution recalls, various compounded oral suspensions, and PharmaTech's docusate sodium oral liquid, which was recalled after Burkholderia cepacia contamination. I cannot supply recall numbers or exact dates with confidence, and the specification cited in each case may differ from what I have described.
answers.A-STABILITY_EXPIRY-topical: Topical recalls driven by stability data that no longer supported the labelled expiry are relatively uncommon compared with sterility or labelling causes. I associate this category with compounded topical creams and with hydrocortisone and clobetasol preparations where assay or preservative content fell out of specification before the expiry date. I do not have specific firms, recall numbers or dates for topical stability-driven recalls that I can state with confidence.
answers.A-STORAGE_DISTRIBUTION-sterile_injectabl: Temperature excursion recalls of sterile injectables typically arise when product is shipped or held outside 2-8 C or above 25 C. I associate this with insulin and biologic products, and with vaccine distribution incidents. For small-molecule sterile injectables, I recall temperature-related actions involving Hospira and Fresenius Kabi products. I cannot give recall numbers, lot codes or initiation dates for these with any confidence.
answers.B-CONTAINER_CLOSURE_DEVICE-ClassIII: Class III container closure and delivery device recalls generally involve defects unlikely to cause adverse health consequences: cracked or leaking bottles, caps that fail torque specification, missing child-resistant features, and dose pumps or droppers that deliver inaccurate volumes. I associate examples with Perrigo, Teva and various generic oral liquid manufacturers, and with metered-dose inhaler actuator defects. I cannot name specific recall numbers or dates reliably.
answers.B-POTENCY_CONTENT-ClassI: Class I recalls for out-of-specification active content are rare but serious. The examples I most associate with this are superpotent compounded preparations, including the 2013 Main Street Family Pharmacy actions, superpotent digoxin tablets, and levothyroxine subpotency actions. I also associate Class I potency actions with epinephrine auto-injectors that failed to deliver the labelled dose. I cannot confirm the classification, recall numbers or dates of any of these from memory.
answers.B-STABILITY_EXPIRY-ClassI: Class I recalls driven purely by stability data failing to support the assigned expiry are unusual, because stability drift more often yields Class II. I am not able to name a specific Class I recall of this type with confidence. Categories where it could arise include life-supporting injectables and emergency-use products such as epinephrine and naloxone, where loss of potency before expiry carries serious risk.
answers.B-UNAPPROVED_MARKETING-ClassII: Class II recalls for distribution without the required marketing authorisation typically involve unapproved homeopathic products, unapproved prescription drugs marketed under grandfathered claims, and imported products lacking an NDA or ANDA. I associate this category with King Bio homeopathic products, with unapproved ear drop and cough preparations, and with various nasal sprays. I cannot state recall numbers or dates with confidence.
answers.C-Amneal_Pharmaceuticals_LLC: Amneal Pharmaceuticals has had multiple recalls. The ones I associate with the firm include nitrosamine impurity actions on ranitidine and metformin extended-release, a recall of levothyroxine and liothyronine tablets for subpotency, and dissolution failures in several oral solid products. I cannot give a complete list, and I cannot supply recall numbers, classifications or dates for these actions with confidence.
answers.C-Eli_Lilly_Company: Eli Lilly recalls I associate with the firm include insulin products, Trulicity pens, and Humalog cartridges. I also associate Lilly with a recall of Cialis and with actions relating to particulate matter in injectable products. I do not have a reliable list of Lilly recall events, and I cannot supply recall numbers, classifications or dates.
answers.C-MYLAN_PHARMACEUTICALS_INC: Mylan Pharmaceuticals has had numerous recalls. Ones I associate with the firm include valsartan and other sartan products recalled for nitrosamine impurities, EpiPen auto-injectors recalled for failure to activate, alprazolam tablets recalled for a foreign substance, and various oral solids recalled for dissolution or labelling failures. I cannot give recall numbers, classifications or dates, and some of these may belong to Mylan Institutional or to Mylan N.V. affiliates rather than to Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc.
answers.C-Pharmalucence_Inc_: Pharmalucence is a sterile injectable and radiopharmaceutical manufacturer based in Bedford, Massachusetts. I associate the firm with recalls of sterile injectable products for lack of sterility assurance and for particulate matter, and with actions relating to its kit products. I cannot name individual recall events, recall numbers, classifications or dates for this firm with any confidence.
answers.D-DISSOLUTION-2013_2015: Dissolution failures in 2013-2015 were a common recall reason for generic oral solids. I associate the period with recalls of metformin extended-release, bupropion extended-release, methylphenidate extended-release (Mallinckrodt and Kudco products, following an FDA bioequivalence review), and various extended-release formulations where release rate drifted on stability. I cannot supply recall numbers, firms or dates for individual events with confidence.
answers.D-DISSOLUTION-2019_2021: Dissolution-driven recalls in 2019-2021 that I associate with the period include extended-release metformin products, several extended-release opioid formulations, and generic oral solids where dissolution drifted during stability testing. I cannot give firms, recall numbers or dates for individual events with confidence, and the nitrosamine actions that dominate my memory of this period were impurity rather than dissolution failures.
answers.D-MICROBIAL_NONSTERILE-2013_2015: Microbial contamination of non-sterile products in 2013-2015 that I associate with the period includes Burkholderia cepacia contamination of oral liquids and mouthwash, and mould or yeast contamination in oral suspensions and topical preparations. I cannot name specific firms, recall numbers or dates for this window with confidence.
answers.D-STABILITY_EXPIRY-2022_2026: I do not have reliable knowledge of individual recall events from 2022 onwards driven by stability data failing to support the assigned expiry. This category generally involves assay or impurity drift observed during on-going stability that invalidates the labelled shelf life. I cannot name firms, products, recall numbers or dates for this period.
answers.E-DISSOLUTION-exUS: Dissolution-driven recalls from firms outside the United States most often involve manufacturing sites in India and China supplying the US generic market. I associate this with sites operated by Aurobindo, Sun Pharma, Lupin, Torrent and Zydus. I cannot name individual recall events, recall numbers or dates with confidence, and I cannot confirm which of these were dissolution failures rather than impurity or GMP actions.
answers.E-GMP_DEVIATION-exUS: CGMP deviation recalls from non-US sites are strongly associated with Indian and Chinese manufacturing facilities that received FDA warning letters or import alerts. Firms I associate with this include Ranbaxy, Wockhardt, Sun Pharma's Halol site, and various Chinese API manufacturers. I cannot supply individual recall events, numbers, classifications or dates with confidence.
answers.E-IMPURITY_DEGRADATION-exUS: Impurity-driven recalls from non-US sites are dominated by the nitrosamine actions beginning in 2018: NDMA and NDEA in valsartan, losartan and irbesartan from Zhejiang Huahai Pharmaceutical in China and from Hetero Labs and Aurobindo in India, and later NDMA in ranitidine and metformin. I cannot supply individual recall numbers, classifications or dates with confidence.
answers.E-MICROBIAL_NONSTERILE-exUS: Microbial contamination of non-sterile products from non-US sites is a category I associate with imported oral liquids, hand sanitisers and topical preparations, particularly from Mexican and Indian manufacturing sites. I cannot name individual firms, recall events, recall numbers or dates for this category with confidence.

I cannot supply a list of individual recall events, recall numbers, classifications or dates with confidence.
